text:
Devin Cooley made 36 saves on 37 shots, and Calgary needed every one of them. The Flames beat Minnesota 2-1 at the Scotiabank Saddledome despite being outplayed for most of the night. Cooley stopped about 2.4 goals more than the shots he faced should have allowed, which is what goals saved above expected measures. The league's three-star panel named him the first star.

Calgary got its goals early and then held on. Aydar Suniev scored on the power play at 10:49 of the first, and Joel Farabee made it 2-0 on another power-play wrist shot at 14:06. The Flames went 2 for 4 with the man advantage, while Minnesota went 0 for 4 on its own chances. Michael McCarron got one back at 4:39 of the third, but that was all the Wild could manage.

The underlying numbers lean hard toward Minnesota. The Wild led in shot attempts 69 to 38 and in expected goals, a measure of chance quality, 3.35 to 2.17. They out-chanced Calgary 2.06 to 0.23 in the third period alone. Minnesota's deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that the Wild win, was 73 percent. Matt Boldy fired seven shots on goal in 25:06, and Joel Eriksson Ek had a 24 percent look in the first period that missed the net. The facts provided don't include streaks or standings for either team, so the result stands as a Calgary win and a Minnesota loss decided mostly by one goalie and two early power plays.
